dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."
"The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My inference is that the cluster reflects scheduled dealer-batch timing."
"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates; the May rows have effective dates from 1–28 May and post on 31 May."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "That inference is strong for duplication and pipeline-integrity questions but does not settle accounting recognition or subscriber fulfilment."
"Material unknown | Evidence needed to resolve it | How that evidence would change my decision"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is one read-only verification query comparing the West-dealer trend by `posted_at` and `effective_event_date`, alongside a small entitlement sample."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the result."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."
"Those two boundaries explain why neither immediate escalation nor unconditional closure is appropriate."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Cross-checking the raw files against operational claims confirms that the 17-row 31-May cluster is an expected month-end batch from West dealers DLR-104 and DLR-219 on contractually permitted terms" — the cited files support the pattern and reconciliation, but no specific contract or source establishing permitted terms is cited, and the causal explanation is not fully proven by the records alone.

"Reconciling dealer settlement cycles against bank remittance logs confirms that funds arrived in accordance with monthly credit agreements without revenue inflation." — bank remittance logs and monthly credit agreements are not identified among the cited supplied sources.

"No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline remediation is warranted." — the entitlement sample and reporting-clock policy were still unresolved, and the submission did not independently test all possible pipeline timestamp or aggregation defects.
"with ... no evidence of billing manipulation" — unique identifiers and reconciliation reduce support for duplicate billing, but they do not by themselves exclude every form of manipulation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A posting-time or aggregation defect could still exist even with unique source_event_id values, complete row acceptance, and zero cash-to-ledger variance; those checks establish reconciliation and uniqueness more directly than they establish that the batch timing was intentionally generated by the dealer process. The submission partly handles this through its event-time query, but does not explicitly test or rule out that pipeline alternative.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and report the actual reconciliation and entitlement-check results, then explicitly recommend that downstream trend and retention analytics use effective_event_date rather than posted_at when measuring event timing. This would convert the currently proposed conditional safeguard into evidence-based closure while preserving the finance conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes."
"Under legacy routing, 49.5% of sessions generated tickets (219/442), whereas NOVA-S1 created tickets for only 3.3% of callers (90/2,709)."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The supplied data cannot distinguish genuine resolution from changed authentication and case-creation measurement."
"I cannot determine whether dropped authentication sessions resulted in callbacks without a read-only 7-day recontact trace."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet; keep the South pilot at its current scope while measuring contacts like-for-like."
"The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Person: Farah Iqbal, Customer Care Operations, because she owns IVR journey stages, case-creation conditions, and the containment definition."
"What written pass threshold and observation window govern pilot-to-national expansion?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "New self-service stages balance_check (29.1% of sessions) and pack_info (21.3%) do not exist at all under legacy routing (0%), representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers." Stage frequencies and authentication status do not establish successful resolution or deflection.

"The 650 pre-authentication drops described in `email-ivr-pilot.eml` represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution." These drops may indicate friction, but abandonment is not itself a complaint or proof of unsuccessful resolution.

"Analysis of `ivr_interactions.jsonl` confirms that the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes." The data strongly supports a changed capture process, but does not establish that this is the sole explanation for the ticket decline.

"South network events in `service_events.csv` remained steady across May and June" is overstated: the cited affected-account figures decline from 9,409 to 7,045, and network events are not expected to move one-for-one with complaints.

"higher repeat contact or no recovery path requires remediation; a low rate supports only another limited evaluation stage." Repeat-contact rates alone do not validate customer experience; linked journey outcomes and sampled call review are also needed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the main alternative that lower tickets could reflect changed case creation rather than improvement, and it preserves genuine resolution as an unknown. It misses a fully developed benign interpretation: some authenticated callers may have successfully completed self-service, while some pre-authentication abandonment may reflect non-complaint callers or transient authentication issues. It also does not sufficiently separate network-event exposure from complaint outcomes.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the assertion that the decline is an artifact or that abandonment is uncaptured friction with an end-to-end validation plan linking IVR sessions to 7-day repeat contacts and downstream outcomes, supplemented by sampled call listening. This would distinguish successful self-service, authentication failure, and non-complaint abandonment before any expansion decision.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and identifies the specific fields `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `event`, `severity`, `duration_min`, `timestamp_local`, and `inverter_id`.
It distinguishes the observed constant fields from the limitation that they cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It compares severity, duration, clearance status, impact, recurrence, and inverter distribution rather than treating the warning label alone as proof of equipment failure.
It tests the innocent explanation that the extract may be incomplete by proposing an unfiltered raw-database query, but it does not triangulate an independent operational or telemetry channel.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly notes that constant fields and the lack of an unfiltered plant baseline limit what can be concluded.
It conditions escalation on finding uncleared faults or nonzero generation losses and avoids claiming that the warning proves active damage.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to 'conduct a single read-only completeness verification' is proportionate, reversible, and directly addresses the stated uncertainty.
The proposed query for 27 May–4 June without status filters is a discriminating next test: it could reveal hidden uncleared or nonzero-impact records without initiating an equipment investigation.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that the four observed events are isolated, self-clearing, and zero-impact is supported by the cited rows and fields.
'Hold escalation' fits the evidence while preserving escalation if the completeness check reveals materially different records.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'Low-severity' is a reasonable characterization of three `info` events and one warning with zero impact, but severity labels alone do not prove operational insignificance.
'Self-resolving' is inferred from `cleared=yes`; the file does not establish why the events cleared or whether the communications condition recurred outside the extract.
'This check is completely safe and reversible' is reasonable for a read-only query, but the submission does not verify database access controls or query scope.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The seven-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` could represent an intermittent communications or telemetry-quality issue rather than an inverter equipment problem. An incomplete export could also hide recurrence or nonzero-impact records; that is why completeness verification is the appropriate limited follow-up.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add one independent cross-check, such as raw event-log coverage or plant/inverter telemetry for the same timestamps, to distinguish a genuinely isolated communications warning from recurrence omitted by the extract.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields in `dispatch_blocks.csv` (`base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source`) and provides reproducible calculations for both the 17.6% modeled estimate and the 31.6% cross-day arithmetic.
It distinguishes the observed arithmetic from interpretation, stating that the same-day result is “descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It identifies the key design problem: “It is a cross-day comparison,” and notes that similar firmware and wind fields do not establish a randomized or fully matched control.

It tests multiple alternatives, including fabrication, causal attribution, metric definition, and commercial value, and rejects them with references to `dispatch_blocks.csv` and `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`.
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May while retaining the distinction between modeled savings and causal impact.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission uses claim-specific confidence: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”

It explicitly identifies unknown selection/timing and repeatability/net value, and states what evidence would change the decision, including pre-outcome timestamps, matched pilot days, and reconciled settlement data.
It avoids both overclaiming and overcorrecting: the 17.6% result is retained as a smaller modeled benefit rather than dismissed entirely.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to keep expansion on hold follows directly from the causal and net-value limitations rather than from an unsupported allegation.

The proposed “prospective shadow validation across pre-registered matched high-wind stow days” is discriminating, prospective, and preserves operational constraints because it changes no submitted schedule or plant control.
It adds the needed commercial measurement: energy revenue at Rs 2.72/kWh, DSM penalty, and pilot costs.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the evidence: “Insufficient evidence that the AI pilot caused a 31.6% improvement,” while acknowledging that the 31.6% arithmetic is reproducible.

It gives the appropriate narrower conclusion that 29 May had a modeled penalty about 17.6% below the retained base schedule against the same realized generation, without treating that as causal proof.
It aligns with the evidence that the pilot day may have performed better while the headline estimate is not a controlled causal estimate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the read-only shadow calculation is “fully reversible” is a reasonable operational characterization but is not directly established by the supplied files.

The statement that the 12 pilot revisions “containing” the submitted schedule caused the modeled difference remains inferential; the submission appropriately labels the result model-based rather than causal.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The favorable 29 May result may reflect day-specific conditions, selection of the comparison date, forecast or scheduling differences, or other non-pilot factors rather than the AI revisions. The same-day base-versus-submitted calculation is useful directional evidence, but because the base schedule is modeled and there is only one pilot day, it cannot isolate the pilot's causal effect.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run the proposed prospective, pre-registered matched-day shadow validation with immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net-settlement accounting, especially pilot cost, energy revenue, and DSM penalty.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"commercial_invoice.pdf confirms P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900 and air_waybill.pdf links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522."
"The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios master data supersedes local declaration filings’: rejected because Helios is commercial data without customs-ruling authority."
"Whole-string comparison cannot establish misclassification."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Swiss Matrix supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation."
"The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."
"A contradictory code flips decision to escalate; 90211000 closes review."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios in product_master_current.xlsx is commercial data, not ruling authority."
"canonical-schema-v0.3.md lacks jurisdiction and version metadata, so direct string comparison cannot prove error."
"Resolving schema deficiencies prevents repetitive false positives across Swiss entries."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Binding classification requires official customs rulings" is a legal/process assertion not supported by a specifically cited source in the submission.
"Swiss Matrix supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation" may be reasonable, but the stated requirement for confirmation is not directly evidenced in the table.
"CHF 126,900 total closes it" is overstated: value presentation may affect valuation or review, but resolving value presentation does not by itself establish the correct tariff classification.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is broad and would be stronger if limited explicitly to the listed evidence and the relevant effective date.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 90211000 entry may be a nonbinding or outdated Swiss reference, or the product may have facts requiring a different Swiss classification on 2025-11-04; in that case the mismatch could represent a genuine declaration error. The submission recognizes this possibility and requests effective Tares or ruling confirmation, but does not independently establish the legal status of the matrix entry.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite and verify the effective Swiss Tares or binding-ruling record for P1001 on 2025-11-04, explicitly distinguishing its legal authority and effective date from the commercial Helios record and the matrix snapshot.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`" and cites `air_waybill.pdf` plus `packet_manifest.txt`.
"IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090" and cites the declaration and line number.
"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31" and cites the specific register fields and shipment date.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference indicator alone validates preferential treatment’: rejected because preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration".
"‘Commercial manufacturing country in commercial_invoice.pdf disproves preference’: rejected because manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preferential origin".
"‘The shipment should be flagged for fraud’: rejected because absence of a supplier declaration ... represents unverified documentation, not intentional misdeclaration."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The claim is unsupported by packet evidence, but not disproved."
"valid supplier declarations may exist in procurement archives."
"Distinguishing unverified documentation from intentional misdeclaration ensures that administrative holds precede any formal compliance escalation."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv` or procurement folders per `origin-workshop.md` is the required proof."
"Identity of the actual sourcing supplier" is linked to a proposed "Sourcing purchase order linking SHP-000411 to a specific supplier ID".
"The packet does not identify which supplier sourced this shipment" and the submission connects that missing linkage to the inability to apply supplier-specific evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place an administrative hold on the Irish preferential tariff claim."
"Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof ... and do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The assertion that preferential origin categorically "requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is not fully established by the cited excerpts; the submission should distinguish the legal proof requirement from this system's evidence-control requirement.

The statement that a valid declaration can be obtained "from `supplier_origin_register.csv`" may overstate what a register provides if it is only an index or status record rather than the underlying supplier declaration.
The statement that "SUP-01 would confirm non-preferential MFN" is insufficiently supported in the submission because the relevant SUP-01 record and its exact status are not quoted.

The submission says absence of a declaration "leads to removing preference claim," but the appropriate correction may depend on the governing preferential-origin rule, duty calculation, and any later supplier evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or a valid declaration may exist in procurement archives but be absent from the packet and ClearView linkage. In that case the preference claim could ultimately be valid; the current evidence supports an administrative hold and verification, not rejection, fraud, or a definitive duty correction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Separate the supplier-origin register's role as an index/status source from the underlying declaration and explicitly quote the governing preferential-origin rule and the relevant supplier records before stating that a declaration is legally required or that preference must be removed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "For 220 completed rows, receipt-to-release mean is 45.5 hours..." cites batch_release.csv fields and completed rows.
"185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00" cites batch_release.csv and source_freshness.csv.
"The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored" cites disposition and timestamp fields.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The SOP clock requires evidence_available_ts, which is missing" separates the target metric from available proxies.
"Using lab_complete_ts as an approximation introduces uncontrolled error" identifies a confounder.

The submission triangulates timestamp concentration, source freshness, missing evidence timing, and right-censoring, although it does not fully test whether any post-evidence workflow delay remains after reconstructing event times.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table labels claims High or Medium-High confidence and states that "missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release."
"The snapshot cannot compute compliance with SOP service targets" appropriately limits the conclusion to the available extract.

The submission recognizes source and censoring limitations, but its statement that timestamps are "defaulted" is stronger than the demonstrated observation of exact concentration at the snapshot boundary.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification" directly changes the decision rather than accepting the headline metric.
It proposes reversible read-only verification and distinguishes redefining the metric from validating it.
The strict routine subset and its 22/23 within-24-hours result provide a useful bounded operational signal while avoiding publication of an invalid headline KPI.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects "The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed" using the 02:10 concentration and rejects "Discard the extract as corrupt" using valid monotonic duration arithmetic.
It also recognizes that incomplete HOLD batches may change the queue-health interpretation.
The strongest alternative—that genuine workflow delay may coexist with interface-timestamp distortion—is not explicitly developed or tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Execute a targeted read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches in live QCore and CertVault" is a small, prioritized next step.
The table specifies what would change the decision for evidence availability, true disposition time, and open HOLD durations.

The request for "live QCore timestamp audit capturing true certificate upload times" should more precisely identify the authoritative evidence-availability and disposition-event logs, rather than relying mainly on spot checks.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not literally supported because evidence_available_ts is missing; this appears to be a lab-complete or other proxy, not an evidence-to-release measure.

The statement that 185 timestamps are "defaulted" or "synthetic snapshot artifacts" is a reasonable inference from exact 02:10 concentration and source freshness, but the extract alone establishes the pattern more directly than the underlying timestamp-generation mechanism.
The claim that reconciling the 42 HOLD rows would change the decision on overall queue health is plausible but conditional; the evidence does not show how long those cases will remain open.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The headline may combine two effects: interface or snapshot timing makes many releases appear late or clustered, while genuine workflow delay after required evidence becomes available may still exist. The current extract cannot determine the relative contribution because it lacks the authoritative evidence-availability and event/decision timestamps.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the proxy language with an explicit timestamp-semantics test: obtain an event-level sample containing required-evidence availability, disposition decision, and QCore interface-commit timestamps for the same batches, with extract timestamps reconciled to a common snapshot. This would distinguish measurement artifact from real post-evidence process delay and determine whether any KPI can safely be published.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The eight actionable request IDs are PR-260701, PR-260706, PR-260708, PR-260710, PR-260711, PR-260718, PR-260721, and PR-260722.”
“The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot.”
“Revision-B valve supply is two free units ... against four units of revision-B demand.” — supported with request, stock, restriction, and freshness files.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity”: rejected,” using reservation and zero-stock evidence.
“Same part family means interchangeable”: rejected,” using revision-A versus revision-B evidence and the substitution rule.
“An expensive semantic-search system is required”: rejected,” based on exact MPN joins for populated requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “‘Actionable now’ still requires current confirmation.”
“The hypothesis survives only if records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check.”
“The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests” is stronger than the stated stale-snapshot caveat supports.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers.”
The submission separates “Actionable now,” “Needs check,” and “Not transferable,” and proposes live CMMS, engineering, and qualification checks.
“Master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority” is a useful reframing but is not fully established for the 11 blank-part-number requests.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission actively tests and rejects automatic transfer, family-level interchangeability, interpreting -1 availability as zero stock, and the need for semantic search.

“What Would Change the Decision” identifies evidence that could revive the rejected interpretations, including live reservation data, engineer approval, and comparison of exact-join versus semantic-search performance.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records.”
“Live local CMMS reservation and availability query.”
“Receiving engineer and qualification approval.”
“Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search.”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “An exact join on manufacturer part numbers succeeds for 100% of populated requests” establishes candidate identity, not that all 13 requests are resolved operationally or transferable.
“An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately” overstates what the join demonstrates because revision, reservation, UOM, qualification, and stale-stock constraints still apply.

“The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests” should be presented as candidate or conditional value, not firm savings, because the global stock snapshot is stale and current availability remains unconfirmed.

“The other 11 requests require master-data hygiene, not an expensive semantic search engine” is not demonstrated: semantic search may still improve recall for requests with blank MPNs, and no measured exact-versus-semantic comparison is provided.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching is a strong precision and candidate-generation baseline, but semantic search may still add material recall for the 11 requests without populated part numbers. The appropriate conclusion is likely a hybrid: use exact MPN joins where available, semantic search for discovery, and require engineering, revision, UOM, reservation, and live-availability confirmation before transfer.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a current, point-in-time CMMS and engineering validation for the eight proposed actionable requests, explicitly checking free quantity, reservation/criticality, revision, qualification, and UOM. Reclassify their $20,536.31 as confirmed, conditional, or rejected value, then benchmark semantic search on the 11 blank-MPN requests for incremental validated recall.
